issuer.name: New Zealand, Chile and Singapore (original Parties)

relevance.reason: A binding digital-economy agreement whose Module 8 contains a dedicated article on artificial intelligence. The AI provision is expressly included in a treaty, although its operative language is cooperative and best-efforts ('shall endeavour'), not a set of prohibitions or product rules.
ai_provisions: Article 8.2 — Artificial Intelligence: recognition of AI's economic and social importance; promotion of ethical and governance frameworks; consideration of internationally recognised principles including explainability, transparency, fairness and human-centred values
relevance.excluded_scope: The AI article does not create enforceable substantive standards, conformity assessment or market-access conditions; it commits the Parties to promote and endeavour.

dates.notes: Signed by New Zealand, Chile and Singapore on 11 June 2020 GMT (12 June 2020 New Zealand time). Entered into force for New Zealand and Singapore on 7 January 2021 and for Chile on 23 November 2021. Korea's accession took effect on 3 May 2024. A Protocol to the DEPA was signed on 15 July 2023; sources differ between 19 and 20 March 2024 for its entry into force.

status_note: In force for New Zealand, Singapore, Chile and Korea. Costa Rica was invited to accede and, according to Singapore's MTI page consulted in this session, joined in September 2026; that accession is recorded as a gap because the depositary record was not read.

parties.summary: Four Parties as of the verification date: New Zealand, Singapore, Chile and Korea. The depositary is New Zealand.
